claims.statement: Both app targets declare the private CloudKit container `iCloud.com.akinokaede.termind`, which the Vault, Settings, Metrics, History and Device coordinators share via CloudSyncContainer.identifier.

Settings retains its zone/subscription and adds native V1 TerminalCustomThemeItem and TerminalThemeSelectionItem. Themes use inline text or raw UTF-8 assets above 700,000 bytes with SHA-256 hashes; selections encode appearance and builtin/custom choice. Tombstones clear live fields; invalid combinations and hashes fail decoding. Tests cover ordering, independent theme merges, native-choice protection from legacy writes, deletion and V56 migration/reopening. Metrics retains its independent zone/type/subscription.
Cloud sync record coding stores payloads inline through 700,000 bytes and uses a CKAsset above that threshold.
SFTP preferences default to 30 global and 10 per-Host transfers with Smart topology; global values are bounded to 1–100, per-Host values to 1–50, and per-Host is clamped to the global value.
The SFTP settings sync store uses a distinct synchronized SFTP preference value and preserves legacy saved limits while defaulting missing values to the current 30/10 configuration.

Vault and Device follow the master iCloud switch; History, Metrics and Settings have independent optional switches, and History defaults on without inheriting the retired Vault selection or environment.

The local V35 stage added independent History journals, importer state and capability checkpoints; V36 removes the retired importer table, V37 adds scoped record/replica presence state and V38 adds durable deletion-handoff and asset-cleanup sidecars without changing the native History/Device cloud record types.

Mixed-version safety tests use fake CloudKit transport to cover scoped blocks across replica identities, compatible-record progress, restored batch/provider filtering, save-conflict quarantine, tombstones and recreation, retry/relaunch, atomic failed-unblock rollback, interrupted fetch persistence, causal deletion handoff and on-disk migration; they do not establish live signed-device delivery.

Scoped decoder-capability changes force a full reread before upload, with checkpoint advancement after successful fetch; unsupported native History/Device records are quarantined as full secure CKRecord archives rather than discarded or turned into defaults.

ConnectionHistory writes native V2 and reads V1/V2, adding mosh and eternalTerminal; Device stays V1. Stable IDs, zone and separate kind-scoped owners remain. Terminal deletion and 250 retention differ from legacy coexistence because no continuous Vault importer runs.

The shared container uses V59 without CloudKit mirroring and excludes migration endpoints V29/V32/V33. V51 adds Snippet color, V52 retires highlighting, V53 sessions, V54 artwork, V55 transports, V56 Wake-on-LAN, V57 themes, V58 creation ordering without invented dates, and V59 separate discovered MCP server description metadata preserving historical MCP server shapes. Successive V50–V59 stages are lightweight and independent of wire formats.

V28's stored Host port, identityID and charset survive V28→V30 as SSH-specific values, while Telnet fields are introduced with disabled and default values; changing historical persisted shapes would jeopardize installed-store compatibility.

Current compatibility tests create historical-schema stores rather than using the retired V28 fixture: V30 retains Telnet enablement, V31 backfills history source device, V31/V34 reopen without importing retired Vault journal entries, and V35 reopens preserving native Device data and bindings after importer removal.
Mobile startup coverage verifies shared schema and an empty in-memory repository, not the retired V28 upgrade/relaunch journey or live signed-device delivery.

Physical-delete batches are built from durable scoped journal mutations, exclude blocked or stale queued operations, cap saves plus deletes at 250, and persist the causal version of each delete before handing it to CKSyncEngine.

On incremental deletion or full-inventory absence, scoped cloud-presence state reconciles a handed-off delete with a newer explicit local incarnation, preserving the newer save; History events remain terminal while other categories can explicitly recreate records.

A deleted zone is reset/recreated, while purged/encrypted-reset zones retire their engine and purge only the scoped category replica. Committed asset-cleanup work remains pending until filesystem removal succeeds and is retried before the next engine is constructed.

An account mismatch pauses category synchronization for explicit confirmation; confirmation resets that category's prior account state and binds the new user before starting a new fetch and permitting uploads.

V39 adds local assistant-model selection, and V40 removes retired category-specific quarantine tables while preserving scoped quarantine and recovery; upgrading a V39 disk store retains scoped blocked state and cloud-presence rows.

Lifecycle startup completes pending purge cleanup and commits a scoped recovery-required fence before zone inspection/creation or construction of an automatically syncing engine; a failed fence save prevents network engine construction.

Fetch start revokes upload authorization; only a completed successful fetch reconciles full inventory and capability checkpoints and reauthorizes sends, while failed fetches keep the recovery fence, and overlapping sends keep it until completion.

A delegate persistence failure rolls back and retires the engine, so late callbacks cannot reauthorize it; an interrupted scope's next startup discards its old cursor and refetches while preserving journal pending intent.

The V37 cloud-presence row retains a legacyDeletion column for shipped-store compatibility, but deletion causality now reads confirmed deletion and the V38 handoff sidecar rather than that retired cleanup intent.

V41 adds persistent notification preferences and V42 adds agent message/conversation provenance and collaboration delivery receipts without changing earlier schema shapes; tests verify V40 notification-preference store upgrade and reopening and V41→V42 preservation of existing Host groups with initially empty collaboration sidecars.

Notification preferences use a distinct Settings cloud record type; local round-trip tests show remote Settings updates apply without echoing, older updates do not overwrite a newer value, and deletion restores defaults.

Across History, Device, Vault, Settings and Metrics, repeated unchanged journal system-field updates and duplicate upload acknowledgement avoid additional SwiftData writes; reopening an interrupted fetch retains quarantined bytes, a recovery fence and local pending intent while a separate compatible edit remains uploadable.
After V42, V43 adds public MCP OAuth configuration, V44 replaces the Host model with SSH enablement and forwarding fields, and V45 replaces the SSH key model with Security Key credential metadata.

Cancellation from a retired operation during pause or account transition is not treated as a persistence failure: the operation is invalidated, its engine is cancelled outside the delegate context, and late completion cannot overwrite replacement status.

Both apps use TermindPersistence.makeContainer for normal local-store creation. Mobile accepts an injected dependencies.container; otherwise it uses memory-only storage when inMemory is true or Hosts are supplied, and Application Support Termind.store for disk storage. macOS uses the factory's default disk configuration outside tests and screenshot demos. Category lifecycle constructs independent private CloudKit transport rather than SwiftData mirroring.

On macOS the shared local-container factory acquires a cross-process store lock before opening or migrating a disk store and retains it for the container lifetime; a concurrent process receives an in-use error instead of opening the same store.

Both app targets' entitlement templates declare CloudKit in iCloud.com.akinokaede.termind and substitute ICLOUD_CONTAINER_ENVIRONMENT and APS_ENVIRONMENT; TFI uses aps-environment and TFM uses com.apple.developer.aps-environment. Both targets select Development/development for Debug and Production/production for Release. These checked-in signing inputs do not establish effective signed capabilities, deployed Production schema, or successful live multi-device synchronization; those require separate release verification.

macOS startup checks for another running application with the same bundle identifier before opening a disk container, rejecting older instances without store-lock support via a database-in-use alert and exit; test/screenshot in-memory startup skips that check.
macOS starts category coordinators only with Pro vault-sync access; mobile additionally requires an active scene. Otherwise coordinators pause without deleting local data.

Writers are Host V8 (read 1/2/4/5/6/7/8), HostGroup V7 (read 1–7), SSHKey V3, Snippet/Metrics V2 and WorkspaceTemplate V2. Managed Hosts cannot encode standalone; providers recheck permission and outgoing journal entries. Older encoders reject lossy creation dates, Wake-on-LAN, transports, artwork and sessions. Artwork tests retain migration/wire checks; session tests reopen disabled V52 data; Snippet V1 rejects color and newer V1 clears it. Replay uses current-writer group records under simulated old capability, not frozen V3.

Current Settings sync retires terminal highlighting: capability/upload/presence handling excludes its kind, fetched/conflict/deletion records are ignored before reconciliation/validation and startup discards inactive uploads. The legacy cloud type/key remain compatibility identities rather than an active new-feature deployment requirement.

The Settings coordinator lifecycle test verifies that acknowledgement of an older theme-selection record leaves a newer local or legacy-reconciled selection pending and queued; the provider returns the current selection and only its acknowledgement clears pending work. Legacy reconciliation can change the payload without changing the logical version.

SFTPSettingsModel persists normalized local edits before publishing preferences or notifying the runtime; failed saves preserve preferences and emit no notification. Remote snapshots notify only on change without saving again, as covered by SFTPSettingsTests.
Legacy SFTP JSON without strategy retains its saved limits and defaults to Smart, while unknown strategy values fail decoding; SFTPSettingsTests covers both cases.

Native theme migration permits untouched baseline seeds to follow an accepted legacy Settings winner without a new user-choice clock; explicit native selections, edits and tombstones protect their appearance, and existing native theme IDs are not overwritten or resurrected. Tests cover rejected legacy winners, per-appearance protection, stable IDs across reopening and rollback of journal, projection and upload intent.
